ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, G, and B are on the same horizontal straight line, A is on the left, B is on the right, and G is in the middle. D is directly below G, and there is a right-angle mark at G, indicating that GD is perpendicular to the horizontal line AB. C, G, and E are on the same slanted line, C is at the upper left, and E is at the lower right. The figure marks ∠AGC = 60°. Reasoning: Because GA and GB are opposite rays, and GC and GE are also opposite rays, ∠BGE and ∠AGC are vertical angles, so ∠BGE = 60°. Also because GD is perpendicular to GB, ∠DGB = 90°. GE is located between GB and GD, therefore ∠DGE = ∠DGB - ∠BGE = 90° - 60° = 30°.
